verseContext: Matthew describes what the visitors from far away did the moment they finally found the child.
title: Visitors Worship the King
subtitle: They came from a long way away, and they were the first to kneel
mainTruth: Jesus is not one nation's King — He is the King of everybody, everywhere. People from far away belong to Him too.

read.title: Read Together
read.text:
A long way east of Bethlehem — many months of travelling away — there were men who studied the sky. They were not Jewish. They did not have the temple or the prophets or the commands. They lived in a different country and spoke a different language.

And one night they saw a new star.

Somehow they knew what it meant: a King had been born. So they packed up and left home and travelled for months, following it, over deserts and hills, all the way to a country they had never seen — to find a King who was not even their own.

First they went to Jerusalem, to the palace, because that is where kings live. They asked King Herod, 'Where is the child who has been born King of the Jews? We have come to worship Him.'

Herod did not like that at all. He was the king. He did not want another one. But his teachers looked in the old scrolls and found a prophet's words: the King would be born in Bethlehem.

So the visitors went on to Bethlehem — and the star stopped over one particular house.

They went in. And there was no palace, no throne, no guards. Just a young child with His mother in an ordinary house.

And they knelt down on the floor.

Think about who these men were. Rich, clever, important, from far away, with nothing to do with Israel at all. And they were the first people in the story to kneel down and worship Jesus.

Then they opened their treasure boxes and gave Him gifts: gold, which you give a king; frankincense, sweet-smelling, which you burn for God; and myrrh, a spice used when somebody dies. Three gifts that said King, and God, and one day He will die for us — though the visitors probably did not know that last part.

God warned them in a dream not to go back to Herod, so they went home a different way, and Jesus was kept safe.

Right at the very beginning, before Jesus could even speak, God made sure the story showed us something: this King belongs to the whole world. Whoever you are, wherever you are from, you can come and kneel down too.
read.childText: Far, far to the east there were men who studied the sky. They were not Jewish. They lived in a different country and spoke a different language. One night they saw a brand-new star, and somehow they knew: a King has been born! So they left home and travelled for months and months, over deserts and hills, to find a King who was not even their own. First they went to the palace in Jerusalem, because that is where kings live. But the old scrolls said the King would be born in Bethlehem. So on they went — and the star stopped over one house. They went inside. No palace. No throne. No guards. Just a young child with His mother in an ordinary house. And they knelt right down on the floor. These rich, clever, important men from far away were the very first people to kneel down and worship Jesus! They opened their treasure boxes and gave Him gold, and sweet-smelling frankincense, and myrrh. Then God warned them in a dream, and they went home a different way, and Jesus was kept safe. Right at the beginning God showed us something: this King belongs to the whole world. Whoever you are, wherever you are from, you can kneel down too.

discuss.title: Talk About It
discuss.question: Who were the first people to kneel down and worship Jesus?
discuss.parentGuide: The new concept is that Jesus is the Messiah for all nations — this is a story about belonging. The point children need is the one the passage goes out of its way to make: the first worshippers were foreigners who had none of the advantages, and they got there before the priests in Jerusalem did. Say that plainly, and say it to your own child about your own family. Retrieve Ruth Finds a Home, where an outsider was welcomed in, and God Calls Abraham, where God promised to bless every family on earth. The three gifts are worth naming slowly — gold for a king, incense for God, myrrh for someone who will die — because they are a whole gospel in three boxes. Herod is in the story but do not dwell on him; 'he did not want another king, so God kept Jesus safe' is enough here.
discuss.familyQuestion: Who could we welcome in that nobody expects?

pray.title: Let's Pray
pray.guidedPrayer: Jesus, You are King of the whole world, and that means You are our King too. Thank You that anybody from anywhere can come to You. We kneel down and worship You today. Amen.
pray.childPrompt: Can you tell Jesus that He is your King?
prayerPoints: Worship Jesus as King, in your own words
Thank God that people from every country belong to Him

remember.title: Remember This
remember.memoryVerse: They knelt down and worshipped Jesus, and gave Him gifts.
remember.tip: Kneel right down on the floor together like the visitors did, put your hands out flat, and say: 'Jesus is for everyone.' Then point at yourself and say: 'Even me!'

doToday.title: Do It Today
doToday.action: Choose one thing you own and give it away, or make a gift for somebody today — the way the visitors gave the best they had brought.
doToday.parentNote: Let it cost them a little. The visitors did not bring spares; they opened their treasure boxes. A gift that costs nothing teaches nothing, and a small real cost is enough at this age.
